niche: homes left empty for at least half of a year, read from each home's daily water meter totals against the occupancy the council tax record declares, for a national housing agency choosing its 2027 pilot area
answer: Orrimouth: 203 homes nobody used for at least 26 of the 52 weeks to 27 September 2026, 44 more than Ellingsea's 159
answer_source: submission.md block 1; generator/figures.json call and call_count
analyst_test: A strong analyst who reads every field and rule correctly, matches each water property to its address and community area, and counts each home's weeks in which it drew no water, or less than a few days of one person's use, names the area whose empty homes are mostly sound-plumbed flats, because every volume rule reads the steady flow of an unfixed leak in an empty home as a household living there.
domain_test: The deciding quantity is each home's weeks without use, which the water industry reads off the meter as void weeks (no consumption, or less than a low volume); a customer-side leak breaks that method's precondition, because it flows through the meter every day an empty home stands, so the measurement-error model splits each home's daily totals into a steady non-use flow, which does not vary from one day to the next, and use, which always does. Swapped for a generic summary of the volume (weekly or yearly totals under any line), the call moves from the area with the neglected leaking empties to the area whose empties have sound plumbing.
layer1: two council tax layouts across Teversby's May 2026 move to a new revenues system: an archive closed at go-live and a new extract whose carried accounts restart at go-live
water company properties matched to gazetteer UPRNs, with unmatched properties carried only by their billing address and postcode
meter exchanges part-way through the year on a continuing property, two rows on the exchange day
estimated daily reads after communication gaps, spread evenly across the gap and flagged by read type

the business rates list keyed by its own BA reference, linked through the gazetteer's cross-reference, a holiday site's cottages under one entry

spine.entity: one day's metered water through one supply point

driver: The decisive quantity is how many units stood unused for most of a period, read through an instrument whose daily totals carry, for some units, a steady flow that has nothing to do with use; any line drawn on the total reads the steady flow as use and drops the unused units it runs through, so each unit's totals are split into the part that repeats from day to day and the part that varies, and only the varying part is use.
driver_concrete: Each home's weeks left empty are read from its own daily water totals as the weeks in which no day rose above the home's own steady flow, not as the weeks it drew under a volume line, because a running cistern or a weeping supply pipe in an empty home records the same litres every day and every volume rule reads it as a household.
stump: A competent analyst counts each home's void weeks from the daily meter totals (no water, or under 300 litres in the week) and names Ellingsea with 161 homes, whose empty homes are mostly sound-plumbed flats; the step that lands it there is reading a leak's steady daily flow as use, which keeps 119 of Orrimouth's 203 unused homes out of its count and leaves Orrimouth fifth at 85.

differentiation.task236: 236 reads a surveillance source's capture against an independent fixed-protocol sample; here no second sample exists and the steady flow is separated inside each home's own daily series by its constancy.
differentiation.task260: 260 widens an interval by resampling both raters and items; here no interval decides, and the call turns on splitting a steady non-use flow from use inside each home's own meter series.
differentiation.task464: 464 v8 corrects a composition of coded free text for unequal recall with a moderation subsample; here there is no coding, no subsample and no recall rate, and the instrument's error is identified by its own signature, a flow that never varies from one day to the next.

notes: Redrawn at the draw: generators G3 (record versus operation, the most literal label) is banned against task399, and G16 with method_or_model_selection repeats a signature spent in eight builds; gate_g decomposition_attribution is the honester label anyway, because the meter's volume is correctly reported and the decisive step splits it between a steady non-use flow and use. stump_strategy population_selection: the decisive step decides which homes are in the population left empty, built from each home's meter history and never from a status word; classification_error would be the other honest label and is banned against task399, and decomposition_attribution as a strategy is banned against task211.
